Outbox coalescing rules: Applied on enqueue, scoped by target_id
Queued: send, New op: edit, Result: Rewrite the send payload with the new body (one op); Queued: send, New op: delete, Result: Drop both; nothing is sent; Queued: send, New op: react, Result: Keep both, in order: the react follows the send; Queued: edit, New op: edit, Result: Keep the last edit; Queued: edit, New op: delete, Result: Drop the edit, keep the delete; Queued: react(add), New op: react(remove), Result: Drop both (same emoji and user); Queued: read(ord=5), New op: read(ord=9), Result: Keep the higher ord (max-register)
Why it's done early: The doc says to build this early. Adding it later means checking every op type against every other op type.
docs/DESIGN.md:1859 (Coalescing table)

reply:
Coalescing (`docs/DESIGN.md:1848`) runs when an op is added to the outbox, and only against ops with the same `target_id`. The doc calls it a correctness requirement, not an optimization. Without it, an `edit` or `delete` could target a message the server has never seen, which leads to 404s or a ghost message.
